scenario: [LEXP.4.2] / [ICOM.9.4] — the `nan` constant in a value position (here a `let` binding, one of the enumerated positions) is a compile error (DS_VALIDATE_NAN_VALUE). NaN must never enter working memory: NaN != NaN breaks fact identity, joins, and refraction, so the compiler rejects `nan` at the door — the compile-plane counterpart of the runtime assert reject (runtime/LEXP.4.2, DS_ERR_NAN_REJECTED, -216). `inf` is NOT rejected (Inf == Inf is a permitted value); only `nan` is reserved. `nan` reaches expression position solely via this reserved math constant (there is no bare nan float literal), so every value position — slot value, let/const, `::` cast target — funnels through the same reject.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    v: Float key

rule r:
    T
->
    let n = nan
    log critical "{n}"
